body_en: Play rhetorical stages in Yezo's parliament using a hand of argument cards. Stages chain into levels, many built around a single bill. Your standing carries from one level to the next.
See what your opponent plans, spend your energy to play cards, then end your turn. The opponent acts, and you draw a new hand.
Push your support up to the threshold before time runs out. The Floor Debate needs {majority} of {seats} seats. Argue your opponent's support down to nothing and you win at once.
You lose if your gaffe meter fills, if time runs out, or if your own support falls to nothing. Losing costs you standing, and usually ends the level.
There is no race. You answer a set of questions, and your tone is judged after the last one. Skipping a question costs you tone.
Stay at or above the threshold at the end of every turn. In some TV debates the threshold rises after each turn, and the stage screen announces the new number.
Committees, Town Halls, Caucuses and Floor Debates make you beat several opponents in a row. A committee resets everything between opponents. The others keep your clock running.
Every card costs energy. Unspent energy does not carry over. Ending a turn without playing a card costs you {pass_penalty} energy next turn.
There are six rhetorical styles. Each room favors some styles and suppresses others. Tap a card to see how this room treats it.
Some cards add to your gaffe meter. Fill it and the debate is lost. The limit changes from room to room, from {gaffe_min} to {gaffe_max}, and is shown on the stage screen.
Guard soaks up attacks, stacks up to {guard_cap}, and carries between turns. Only an attack takes it, and it is spent stopping one.

In rooms that ask questions, every card you play in a turn answers that turn's question. A card in the style the question invites gets a boost and pleases the organizations it concerns, while a weak answer reduces your card and annoys them. Lift a card, or tap it once, to preview what it would do to each organization before you play it.

Constituency support, Reputation, Funds and Party support are your four standings, and stages move them. If Constituency support or Party support falls very low, an urgent level (a Town Hall or a Party Steering Committee check-in) appears at the top of the level list, and it is forced on you after your next level if you leave it. If Party support reaches zero, your Funds stop coming in.

Every organization keeps a standing with you. Strong answers please the organizations a question concerns, weak ones annoy them, and some answers set rivals back; organizations you neglect drift back toward where they started. A high standing lets you take an organization's backing in Boosters and may bring a sponsored bill.
XP buys Rhetoric Training sessions, where you draw a card and decide whether to learn it. A Training Session Coupon gives you one draw free. Build your deck on the deck screen.

Spend Funds and XP on supplies and hires that help you in a stage or across a whole level. Tap a staff member to see what each rank gives before you hire. Some supplies pressure organizations instead, so read an item before you use it.

Office Hours are conversations with visitors, and each answer can raise some organizations and lower others. A Floor Vote is a single Aye, Nay or Abstain decision, and a bill passes only when its Aye votes reach a majority of the whole house ({majority} of {seats}). A bill you vote on becomes law and is recorded in Your Record.

The game saves after each stage. Reopen it mid-level and you can resume or abandon the level, and a stage in progress starts over. Administration lets you keep one separate backup to save to and load from.

heading_en: Card numbers change as you play
body_en: The numbers on a card are worked out again after every card you play, so what a card shows is what it will do right now. Boosts and discounts from one card apply to your next card this turn only, and some cards give extra only while your gaffe meter is clean or while you are behind. Cards aimed at one audience can give extra as that audience grows in the room, and Room rules shows the mix.

heading_en: Why a card is bigger or smaller
body_en: Two things scale a card's gain and how hard it hits your opponent: the room and the question. A room favors some rhetorical styles and holds others back, and a question boosts the style it invites and reduces a poor answer; guard, drawing and gaffes are never scaled. Tap a card for a plain-words reading, and a greyed-out card does nothing here right now.

heading_en: Who is pleased by which style
Taking a side on a bill
body_en: In a level about a bill you choose to lean Support or Oppose before it begins. Winning stages pushes your side's organizations up and the other side's down, and your vote then moves them again. Switching sides costs the side you abandon, and going against your party costs Party support.

When an organization thinks highly enough of you, it may ask you to carry a bill under Sponsored Bills in the level list. You can carry it, swap one of its parts, or decline at a cost to its standing. No sponsored bill passes on its own: you need enough influence to swing other parties.

Draft a Bill lets you combine two or three parts from any organizations into a bill of your own, for XP and Funds. Optional stages before the vote let you visit a member to win a seat, and meet a lobbyist who may trade you help for dropping one part. You can carry only one drafted bill at a time.

Each of the six parties rates you from your votes and from how the organizations tied to it feel about you, and the Parties page shows its allies and rivals. Pleasing a rival organization can lower a party's opinion of you. Your own party's opinion drives the urgent levels and the influence you need to swing a vote.
Winning over somebody undecided costs one point; somebody already against you costs one, two or three. You find out which as you go, and points you cannot spend are lost.

Some Tier 1 and Tier 2 cards make you discard other cards from your hand, either to play them or to cycle your hand for new ones. You choose which cards to throw away, and you can cancel before you confirm. They cannot be played in a room that does not refill your hand.
